toc.title: Git, GitHub and the course map

html:
1Git, GitHub and the course map

Git is a distributed version control system: it records the history of a project on your computer. Distributed means every clone holds the whole history, so you can commit, branch and read the log with no network. GitHub is a service that hosts Git repositories and adds pull requests, issues and Actions. The figure is the course map.

Git GitHub
What it is A tool that records history A service that hosts repositories
Where it lives On your computer On the web
Needs a network Only to share work Yes
Gives you Commits, branches, merges Pull requests, issues, Actions
Works alone Yes No, it hosts Git repositories
Tip

. Git works without GitHub, but GitHub does not work without Git. Learn the Git model first: every GitHub feature is built on it.

The course has 17 modules in six parts. The first two parts need no account at all.

Part Modules Topic
1 Foundations 0 to 2 Setup, mental model, daily loop
2 Branching and history 3 to 6 Branches, merging, rebase, undo
3 Working with remotes 7 Clone, fetch, pull, push
4 GitHub collaboration 8 to 12 Pull requests, strategies, protection
5 Automation and safety 13 to 15 Actions, CI, security
6 Practice 16 Recipes and a team capstone

2Install check and first-time configuration

Check the install with git --version. Use Git 2.28 or later: the course uses git init -b main, git switch and git restore. The lab used Git 2.50.1. In this course, the lab means the practice repositories built for the examples: every command shown was run there, and the output you see is real.

Git writes your name and email into every commit, so set them once. Do every Try it block in a sandbox folder, a throw-away place where no real project can be harmed.

git --version
mkdir shopfront
cd shopfront
git init -b main
git status

git version 2.50.1.windows.1
Initialized empty Git repository in .../shopfront/.git/
On branch main

No commits yet

nothing to commit (create/copy files and use "git add" to track)
Setting What it controls Typical value
user.name Name stored in each commit Ada Lovelace
user.email Email stored in each commit Your own address
init.defaultBranch First branch of new repositories main
core.editor Program that opens for messages nano or your editor

On your own machine you set these once for every repository, for instance git config --global user.name. The Try it blocks use --local so that the settings stay inside the sandbox repository.

git config --local user.name "Ada Lovelace"
git config --local user.email "ada@example.com"
git config --show-origin --get user.name
git config --show-origin --get user.email

file:.git/config	Ada Lovelace
file:.git/config	ada@example.com

3Configuration levels and line endings

Git reads settings from three files, and the most specific level wins.

Level Flag Applies to Stored in
System --system Every user of the computer The Git install folder
Global --global You, in every repository .gitconfig in your home folder
Local --local One repository .git/config

git config --list --show-origin prints every setting and its file. Add --show-scope to see the level too. git config --get user.name prints the winning value, and --unset removes a setting.

The output below comes from a lab where all three levels set the same key. On your machine you will usually see global and local lines only.

git config --list --show-origin --show-scope | grep user.name

system	file:.../etc/gitconfig	user.name=System Sam
global	file:.../home/.gitconfig	user.name=Global Gina
local	file:.git/config	user.name=Ada Lovelace
Tip

. When a setting surprises you, ask Git where it came from with --show-origin. The output names the winning value and its file.

Line endings differ by system: Windows ends lines with CRLF, macOS and Linux with LF. Mixed endings make every line look changed in a diff. core.autocrlf is a personal setting, and the Windows installer defaults to converting.

Setting On commit On checkout
autocrlf true CRLF becomes LF LF becomes CRLF
autocrlf input CRLF becomes LF Nothing changes
autocrlf false Nothing changes Nothing changes

With true, Git warns that LF will be replaced by CRLF the next time it touches a file.

The team-wide answer is a .gitattributes file in the repository. The line * text=auto stores text files with LF for everyone who clones, whatever their personal setting. A line such as *.sh text eol=lf keeps LF in the working tree too, which shell scripts need on Windows.

printf '* text=auto\n' > .gitattributes
printf 'one\r\ntwo\r\n' > f.txt
git add .gitattributes f.txt
git ls-files --eol f.txt

i/lf    w/crlf  attr/text=auto  	f.txt

The i/ part is what the repository stores, w/ is the file in your folder.

4First repository, status and help

git init -b main creates the hidden .git folder and names the first branch. Without -b, the name comes from init.defaultBranch, and with neither, Git 2.50.1 still starts on master. The -b flag wins over the setting.

git status is the command you will run most. In the new repository it says On branch main, No commits yet and nothing to commit, and it suggests the next step when files appear.

Tip

. Start every repository with git init -b main. The branch name then never depends on one computer's settings.

Help is built in:

Command What you get
git help status The full manual page
git status -h A short usage summary in the terminal
git help -a Every available command
git help -g Concept guides such as everyday and glossary

5Practice Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Ada's new laptop has no Git identity yet. She wants every repository she creates on it to record her name and email. What should she run?

  • Agit config --local for the name and email in each new repository
  • Bgit config --system for the name and email, as an administrator
  • Cgit config --unset for the name and email, then create a repository
  • Dgit config --global for the name and email, once on the laptop
Show the answer

Answer: D. The global level applies to your user in every repository, so one setting covers all of Ada's future repositories.

S2The config listing shows global ... user.name=Global Gina and local file:.git/config user.name=Ada Lovelace. Which name is stored in the next commit made in this repository?

  • AAda Lovelace, because the local level wins over the global level
  • BGlobal Gina, because the global level wins over the local level
  • CBoth names, because Git joins the values from every level it reads
  • DNeither name, because the system level must confirm the value first
Show the answer

Answer: A. The most specific level wins, and the local level is the most specific.

S3Bob runs git init in a new folder on a computer with no Git settings. git status says "On branch master", but his team uses main. Which command would have started on main?

  • Agit init --main
  • Bgit init -b main
  • Cgit init main
  • Dgit init --branch
Show the answer

Answer: B. The -b flag names the first branch and wins over any setting.

S4A team works on Windows and Linux. Diffs show every line changed in files that a Windows developer touched. What is the most reliable fix for the whole team?

  • AAsk each developer to set core.autocrlf the same way on every machine
  • BAsk the Windows developers to switch to an editor that always writes LF
  • CAdd a .gitattributes file with * text=auto and commit it to the repository
  • DSet core.autocrlf to false in the system configuration of one server
Show the answer

Answer: C. A committed .gitattributes travels with the repository, so every clone gets the same rule whatever the personal settings.

S5Cy runs git status in a folder he just initialized. It prints "On branch main", "No commits yet" and "nothing to commit". What does this tell him?

  • AThe repository exists, has no history yet and has no files to record
  • BThe initialization failed because the folder has no remote repository
  • CThe repository is damaged and needs git init to be run a second time
  • DThe repository has history, but all of its commits are hidden for now
Show the answer

Answer: A. This is the normal state of a new empty repository, not an error.

S6Cy is on a train with no network. In his existing clone, which task can he still do completely?

  • AOpen a pull request, ask for a review and merge it on the website
  • BStart an Actions workflow that builds and tests the latest commit
  • CClose an issue by merging a branch into the default branch online
  • DCommit changes, create branches and read the project history
Show the answer

Answer: D. Git is distributed: every clone holds the whole history, while pull requests, issues and Actions need GitHub.

5.2 Recall questions

R1What does "distributed" mean for Git?

Show the answer

Every clone holds the whole history of the project.

R2Which command lists every setting and the file it comes from?

Show the answer

git config --list --show-origin.

R3Which configuration level wins when a key is set at several levels?

Show the answer

The most specific one: local.

R4Which command creates a repository whose first branch is main?

Show the answer

git init -b main.

R5Name two things GitHub adds around Git.

Show the answer

Any two of pull requests, issues and Actions.

R6Which command prints a short usage summary of git status in the terminal?

Show the answer

git status -h.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Git and GitHub Git records history on your computer; GitHub hosts repositories and adds pull requests, issues and Actions
Install check git --version; use 2.28 or later
Identity user.name and user.email go into every commit
Levels system, global, local; the most specific wins
Inspect git config --list --show-origin, add --show-scope for the level
Line endings autocrlf true, input, false; share the rule with .gitattributes and * text=auto
First repository git init -b main, then git status
Help git help, git status -h, git help -a, git help -g
Practice Work in a sandbox folder and use --local settings
